subject: Road-to-Close: Acceptance signals, sampling plan & fail-safes
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@healthsync.com>, PilotOps <pilotops@healthsync.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 03 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Road-to-Close: Acceptance signals, sampling plan & fail-safes

Hi Elena / HealthSync team —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our working MAP (HS-MAP-v0.9.xlsx) and a short sampling plan that lays out how we'll validate acceptance signals during the 6-week pilot. High level ask: can you review the acceptance signals section and confirm the three primary success criteria by EOD Wednesday PST so we can lock the test owners and target dates?

TL;DR (what we need from you)
- Confirm the three primary success metrics: 1) 96% retrieval precision for named-entity answers (sampling-based), 2) average LLM latency <= 220ms at 95th pctl under pilot traffic, 3) no PII leakage events in the sample audits.
- Assign a HealthSync test owner for each metric and approve the sample cadence (see acceptance-sampling-plan.md).
- Confirm whether Procurement needs any explicit evidence artifacts beyond the trial artifact list (procurement@healthsync.com cc'ed).

Key pieces in the MAP (tab list in the XLSX):
- Milestones: Kickoff, Instrumentation complete, Baseline runs, Controlled sample audits, Final acceptance review.
- Exit gates: pass on the three primary metrics OR documented mitigations + go/no-go executive sign-off.
- Fail-safes: automatic fallback to smaller model variant + extended cache window if latency breach persists.

Attachments: HS-MAP-v0.9.xlsx (MAP master), acceptance-sampling-plan.md (sampling size, randomization, and audit steps).

Planned timeline (proposed)
- Aug 4: HealthSync test owners assigned
- Aug 6-8: Instrumentation and baseline capture
- Aug 11-29: Sampling window & weekly checkpoints
- Sep 2: Acceptance review (decision meeting)

If any of those dates are a hard no, flag them here and we'll adapt.

Thanks — I'll slot a 30-min sync on Thursday in case you want to walk the MAP together.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@healthsync.com>, HealthSync Procurement <procurement@healthsync.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Aug 2025 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Road-to-Close: Acceptance signals, sampling plan & fail-safes

Quick internal notes before the Thursday walkthrough:

Marissa — solid start. Two areas I'd like us to tighten before the client confirms:
1) Sampling detail: for the NER precision metric let's make the sample stratified by document type (claims, notes, lab results) and include at least 300 labeled spans total (see acceptance-sampling-plan.md). That gives us ~3% margin of error at expected precision.
2) Latency test: add a synthetic spike test (10% traffic amplification for 3 minutes) to surface tail behaviors; define the rollback trigger at sustained 95th pctl > 350ms for 2 consecutive runs.

I'll drop a redline into the MAP spreadsheet tonight and add the rollback runbook snippet to the attachments. Ben — can you confirm the quantization profile we'll suggest for the smaller model variant (fallback) so we can list expected quality delta?

Vivek
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <elena@healthsync.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthSync Procurement <procurement@healthsync.com>, PilotOps <pilotops@healthsync.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Aug 2025 10:54:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Road-to-Close: Acceptance signals, sampling plan & fail-safes

Thanks Marissa — the MAP looks pragmatic and I like the explicit fail-safes. A few quick confirmations from our side: 

- Primary metrics: we confirm the three metrics as written. Test owners: I'll assign Priya (Clinical Ops) to NER sampling, and Sam (Infra) to latency; Procurement will shepherd evidence needs (procurement@healthsync.com).
- Sampling cadence: the stratified approach is good. Priya will validate the 300-span floor and may push to 400 depending on document variance; she will let you know by Friday.
- Evidence: Procurement requests exported sample audit logs (CSV export) + a short narrative that ties each failed sample to remediation actions. Doc link or signed checklist is fine.

We agree with the latency spike test. For the rollback trigger, we need clarity on customer-visible impact wording (e.g., "user-facing degraded" vs "internal latency exceedance"). Can we craft wording that ties to product experience (some users see delay > 1s)?

We'll be ready to start instrumentation Aug 6 but need a 1-hour kickoff with PilotOps to validate the tracing headers and sample extraction. Can you do Aug 6 at 1pm PST?

—Elena
Director, Clinical Programs
HealthSync

Date: Wed, 06 Aug 2025 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Road-to-Close: Acceptance signals, sampling plan & fail-safes

Elena — great, thanks for the quick confirmation and for assigning owners. Notes / next steps from my side: 

- Aug 6 1:00pm PST kickoff confirmed with PilotOps — I've sent the calendar invite to Elena, Sam, and our infra lead (Ben).
- Marissa action: update MAP with stratified sampling and add explicit wording for the customer-visible rollback: "If >1% of live users experience response time > 1s for two consecutive 15-min windows, trigger canary rollback and exec notification."
- Ben: please attach the smaller-variant quantization delta estimates in the MAP before the kickoff.
- Procurement: we'll prepare CSV export examples and a 1-page narrative template for evidence; Marissa/Procurement to sync Fri 11am PST if that works.

I'll upload HS-MAP-v1.0 after the kick-off and circulate for final sign-off. Thanks everyone — see you at 1pm.

—Marissa

marissa@redwood.com
